name: Frozen shoulder
goal: Ease pain early on, then steadily win back movement and strength. Frozen shoulder usually recovers, but slowly (often over many months); regular, gentle work helps you get there with less pain and stiffness.
whoFor: People diagnosed with frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis): a painful shoulder that has become stiff in every direction, especially turning the arm outwards.
notFor: Shoulder pain after a fall or injury that hasn't been checked
Recent shoulder surgery: follow your surgeon's or physio's protocol
Pain mainly when lifting the arm while movement is otherwise full (more likely a rotator cuff problem)
trackedMetric: Pain when reaching up or behind your back (0-10)
painRules: Painful stage: move only into mild discomfort, and any ache should settle within about 30 minutes. Later stages: stretching to about 3-4 out of 10 is OK if it settles within an hour and the shoulder isn't worse the next day.
redFlags: Shoulder or arm pain with chest pain, breathlessness, sweating or feeling faint (call emergency services)
Pain or loss of movement after a fall or injury
A red, hot, swollen shoulder, or fever
Numbness, tingling or weakness in the arm or hand
Unexplained weight loss, or a history of cancer

phases.name: Calm the pain
phases.durationHint: often weeks to a few months
phases.entryCriteria: Pain is the main problem: the shoulder aches at rest, wakes you at night and hurts with most movements.
phases.exitCriteria: For about 2 weeks the pain has been calmer (you're sleeping better) and stiffness is now the main problem.

items.note: Very gentle in this stage: only into a mild stretch.

phases.name: Win back movement
phases.entryCriteria: Stiffness is the main problem; pain is mostly at the end of movements.
phases.exitCriteria: Movement is clearly coming back week by week and pain is low (about 2 out of 10 or less).

items.note: A gentle warm-up before the stretches.
Mark your highest point to see progress.

phases.name: Rebuild strength
phases.durationHint: until movement and strength feel normal
phases.entryCriteria: Movement is coming back steadily and pain is low.
phases.exitCriteria: Near-full, comfortable movement and enough strength for daily tasks and sport.

references: Kelley MJ, et al. 2013. Shoulder pain and mobility deficits: adhesive capsulitis. Clinical practice guidelines. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(5):A1-A31.
